sources.entry: mypy - A static type checker for Python.

summary.one_liner: Mypy is a static type checker for Python that finds type errors in type-hinted code without running it.
summary.what_it_does: Checks Python programs annotated with type hints (PEP 484) and reports misuse of variables and functions before the code runs. Supports type inference, generics, callable types, tuple types, union types, and structural subtyping, according to the README. Uses gradual typing, so type hints can be added incrementally and untyped code still runs. Offers a daemon mode (dmypy) for faster incremental re-checks on large code bases. The README lists integrations with VS Code, Vim (Syntastic or ALE), Emacs (Flycheck), Sublime Text, PyCharm, IDLE, and pre-commit. Mypyc, which compiles type-hinted Python to C extensions, is also described; mypy itself is compiled with it.
use_cases: catch type errors in Python code before running it
add gradual type hints to an existing code base
speed up type checking on large projects with daemon mode
integrate static type checking into an editor or IDE
run type checks as a pre-commit hook
notable: Gradual typing: add hints slowly and fall back to dynamic typing where needed
Daemon mode (dmypy) for sub-second incremental updates, per the README
Self-compiled with mypyc, reported as about 4 times faster than interpreted
Editor integrations across many IDEs and editors
caveats: Pre-commit mirror limits analysis of third-party dependencies by default, according to the README
Type hints are not enforced at runtime; the interpreter still runs code with reported errors
